clue.text: Wine in a porous holder; that's ominous !

indicators.note: the wine is placed in the middle of the porous holder, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: tent is an old name for a deep-red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: Someone keeps wine in a leaky vessel, a bad sign for the vintage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wine' wants to be PORT, but the wine here is TENT, an old word for a Spanish red; 'in a porous holder' puts it inside the word POROUS itself, which acts as the holder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something portentous is full of foreboding, a synonym for threatening or ominous.

clue.text: It's dotty' to dance

explanation.walkthrough: 'dotty' is not mad here: it means covered in spots.
explanation.definitionFit: A fabric with regular spots is called polka-dot, and the word is also a lively Bohemian dance.

clue.text: Pull for the shore, my boy !

parts.note: to pull an oar is to row
the shore is land

explanation.surface: A father urges his son to row for the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the' simply links the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a boy's name, fitting the address to a son.

clue.text: Whom Orpheus half regained

parts.note: in Greek myth the musician led his wife almost out of the underworld before looking back and losing her

explanation.walkthrough: Orpheus won his wife back from Hades but lost her by looking back, so he only half regained her.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth she was the wife the musician nearly brought back from the dead.

clue.text: Saw that? Up with no net

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading the words from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: A tightrope walker goes up without a safety net, and onlookers gasp.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenon saw is a fine-toothed saw used for joinery, so 'Saw that?' asks which kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon saw is the woodworking saw named after this joint projection.

clue.text: No applause, not a drink? No wonder one is low!

definitions.text: No applause, not a drink? No wonder one is low!

parts.words: No applause, not a drink? No wonder one is low!
parts.note: receiving no cheers, and having had no cheering drink either, would leave one feeling down

explanation.walkthrough: 'cheer' here is both applause and a drink that lifts the spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Without cheers or applause, and also not cheered up, as a drink might do.

clue.text: Lily among those in haloes

indicators.note: the letters wanted sit among those of the following word, so it is a run inside it

explanation.surface: A white lily appears among saints wearing their golden haloes.
explanation.walkthrough: Aloes were classed in the lily family in older botany, which is why 'Lily' can define it.
explanation.definitionFit: The aloe was traditionally placed in the lily family, so it serves as an example of a lily.

clue.text: Effective way to make Daniel a celebrity ?

definitions.text: Effective way to make Daniel a celebrity ?

parts.words: Effective way to make Daniel a celebrity ?
parts.note: Daniel was thrown among big cats in the Bible, and the verb for treating someone as a celebrity contains those cats

explanation.walkthrough: Daniel was thrown into the lions' den; the verb for making someone a celebrity has lions in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat someone as a celebrity is to make much of them, and the Bible's Daniel was famously put among big cats.

clue.text: "She's great" they said of Diana

parts.note: in Acts 19 the crowd at Ephesus shouted 'Great is Diana' of their city

explanation.walkthrough: The Bible's Acts 19 has the crowd chanting 'Great is Diana of the Ephesians'.
explanation.definitionFit: The people of Ephesus, from Acts in the Bible, cried 'Great is Diana of the' city's people.

clue.text: "He's fat and of breath " (Hamlet)

parts.note: the queen's line in Hamlet about her son during the duel, with a word missing

explanation.walkthrough: The missing word in Gertrude's line from Hamlet's final scene means short.
explanation.definitionFit: A fill-in from Shakespeare: Gertrude says Hamlet is fat and short of breath.

clue.text: Inferior moo-cow ?

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is read as LOW-ER, one who lows, the noise cattle make.
explanation.definitionFit: Lower means of lesser rank or inferior; and a cow that moos lows, so a moo-cow is one that lows.

clue.text: Then clock-making provides the stock answer

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are worked into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clockmaker's output turns out to be the standard reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock answer' reads as a pat reply, but 'stock' alone is the definition: a stock is a wide cravat; 'provides the ... answer' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock was a stiff wide band worn round the neck, a kind of cravat or neck scarf.

clue.text: He's left with the wreck

parts.note: in marine insurance an owner abandons a wrecked ship to the insurer, who is then the person it is handed over to

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a sad castaway, but the term is legal: the insurer takes over the wreck when the owner gives it up.
explanation.definitionFit: In marine insurance the underwriter receives an abandoned wreck, being the party to whom it is surrendered.

clue.text: Hard they are and fast they make

definitions.text: Hard they are and fast they make

parts.words: Hard they are and fast they make
parts.note: things proverbially as hard as can be, which also hold two pieces of wood fast

explanation.walkthrough: Two idioms combine: 'hard as nails' and to nail something fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal spikes are proverbially hard, as in the idiom about a tough person, and they fasten wood together.

clue.text: Straws in the wind, or showers ?

explanation.walkthrough: 'showers' is read as SHOW-ERS, things that show, not rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Straws in the wind are signs of what is coming, and things that show something can be called signs or pointers.

clue.text: Such distinctions excite envy

parts.note: unfair distinctions provoke resentment, and the Latin root of the adjective means envy

explanation.walkthrough: The word comes from Latin invidia, envy; 'invidious distinctions' is a set phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinctions likely to cause resentment are described with this adjective, from Latin for envy.

clue.text: Prescribed wear for a sleuth ? Of course

definitions.text: Prescribed wear for a sleuth ? Of course

parts.words: Prescribed wear for a sleuth ? Of course
parts.note: a sleuth tracks people, so his outfit would be a suit for tracking; and the athlete's outfit is worn on the running course

explanation.walkthrough: A sleuth tracks suspects, so 'his' suit is for tracking; 'Of course' points to the running track.
explanation.definitionFit: The loose outfit worn by athletes for training, read as a suit for a detective who tracks people.

clue.text: "To thine own self be true "---that's the girl!

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation from Hamlet supplies 'true'; in Latin the feminine of true is the girl's name, fitting 'own self' addressed to a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for true, in its feminine form, is also a girl's name.

clue.text: Make a wampum disbursement

parts.note: wampum was shell-bead money of Native Americans, so paying with it means handing out shells

explanation.walkthrough: Wampum is strings of shell beads once used as money by Native Americans.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay up money, read literally as handing out shell beads, the Native American currency.

clue.text: Goodbye in pastoral setting

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is the Latin farewell; the other the poetic valley.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin farewell, used in English; and a poetic word for a valley in the countryside.

clue.text: Poplar street ?

parts.note: a tall narrow poplar tree takes its name from a north Italian region, as does a famous banking street in the City of London

explanation.walkthrough: Lombard Street is the historic banking street in the City of London; Poplar is also a district of East London, a further distraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lombardy poplar is a tree and Lombard Street the London banking street, both named after the north Italian region.

clue.text: Binders of gentlemen's agreements are sometimes golden

definitions.text: Binders of gentlemen's agreements are sometimes golden

parts.words: Binders of gentlemen's agreements are sometimes golden
parts.note: the gesture that seals an informal deal between gentlemen, and the golden payoff given to a departing executive

explanation.walkthrough: A golden handshake is the British term for a generous payoff on leaving a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Clasping hands seals an informal deal, and a 'golden' one is a large payment to a departing executive.

clue.text: It's youthfully capricious, pretending like this

definitions.text: It's youthfully capricious, pretending like this

parts.words: It's youthfully capricious, pretending like this
parts.note: a young goat skips about capriciously, and the word for teasing or pretending also describes a goat giving birth

explanation.walkthrough: A kid is a young goat; 'capricious' comes from Latin caper, goat, so 'youthfully capricious' points to goats.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means teasing or joking, and a young goat (Latin caper, hence capricious) gives birth in this way.

clue.text: This blow-out is the end !

parts.note: a blow that puts a boxer out, ending the fight

explanation.walkthrough: Add 'out' to the blow and you have the knockout that ends a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow or rap; a punch followed by 'out' ends a boxing bout.

clue.text: He leads the world astray, in France at least

definitions.text: He leads the world astray, in France at least

indicators.note: the letters wander off from their proper order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: monde is the French word for world, signalled by 'in France'

explanation.surface: The devil is the great misleader of humankind, at least according to the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in France' says to put 'world' into French, MONDE, which 'astray' rearranges; the whole clue also describes the tempter.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiend or devil is the being who tempts mankind into wrongdoing.

clue.text: Information essential to the brinkman

parts.note: a man walking at the edge of a cliff must be aware of the ledge he stands on

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as KNOW LEDGE: the man on the brink needs to know where the ledge is.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts and learning are what the word means, and split it reads as being aware of a ledge.

clue.text: With wild oats one has old port

indicators.note: the letters run wild, so they are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A young man sowing wild oats comes ashore at an ancient harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' and 'has' link: 'wild' rearranges OATS together with I for 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostia was the ancient harbour town of Rome at the mouth of the Tiber.

clue.text: What happened with an East wind over the Channel

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
vent is French for wind, the language across the English Channel

explanation.surface: Something occurred when an easterly blew across the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over the Channel' means in France, so 'wind' becomes the French word for it.
explanation.definitionFit: An occurrence or happening is what the word means.

clue.text: By reason of the way the deposit is paid

definitions.text: the way the deposit is paid

explanation.walkthrough: A deposit is money paid in advance, as part of the total, which is paying 'on' the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means because of; and a deposit is a payment made in part, ahead of the full sum.

clue.text: Her side of the family want peace

definitions.text: Her side of the family want peace

parts.words: Her side of the family want peace
parts.note: a woman's name, and the branch from this tree is offered as a token of peace

explanation.walkthrough: 'side of the family' suggests a branch; holding out a branch from this tree is a peace offering, and it is also a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name; the branch of this tree held out is a symbol of seeking peace.

clue.text: But even modest billiard-players put it on

definitions.text: But even modest billiard-players put it on

parts.words: But even modest billiard-players put it on
parts.note: putting this on means giving yourself airs, and at billiards it is the spin given to a ball

explanation.walkthrough: Modest people would not 'put on airs', yet billiard players impart spin to the ball, which carries the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on airs is an idiom for showing off, and at billiards the word means spin applied to the ball.

clue.text: In this way the state might resemble a pressure cooker

indicators.note: says the following words, rearranged in a certain way, give the answer

explanation.surface: Under pressure, a nation could start to resemble a kitchen pan about to blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In this way' tells you to rearrange STATE MIGHT; the result describes a sealed pressure cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressure cooker is sealed so that no vapour escapes, which is what the word describes.
